title: Which adjacent gate could explain two population measurements?
assumptions: The sites \(0,\ldots,N-1\) are arranged on a line, with \(N\ge2\). The input is a real unit vector \(x\). Two exact population reports \(p,q\) have nonnegative entries summing to one, with \(p_j=x_j^2\). The input signs are unreported.

The proposed explanation is exactly one operation on an edge \((i,i+1)\). On that ordered pair it applies \(R(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}\cos(\theta/2)&-\sin(\theta/2)\\ \sin(\theta/2)&\cos(\theta/2)\end{pmatrix}\) for an arbitrary real \(\theta\), fixing every other coordinate.
conventions: The angle may be zero. An explanation need only reproduce the output populations \(q_j\); no output signs are specified.
Write \(P_k=\sum_{j=0}^{k}p_j\) and \(Q_k=\sum_{j=0}^{k}q_j\) for the mass to the left of the cut between \(k\) and \(k+1\), where \(0\le k<N-1\).
question:
Using the two lists of cut masses, find every edge on which one gate could have produced the second report. Give a necessary and sufficient test and justify it for every choice of signs consistent with \(p\), allowing the angle to depend on the actual input. Explain what the test says when the reports agree and when the input has zero mass on the proposed pair.

For \(N=4\), suppose \(p=(1,2,1,4)/8\). Diagnose each proposed output \(q^{(1)}=(1,1,2,4)/8\) and \(q^{(2)}=(2,2,1,3)/8\). For each, give all possible edge locations or explain why no single gate fits.

title: How many adjacent rotations prepare one signed state?
assumptions: Let \(N\ge1\). The real coordinate sites of a path are \(0,\ldots,N-1\). The known target \(x\in\mathbb R^N\) has \(\sum_jx_j^2=1\). Its support is \(S=\{j:x_j\ne0\}\). The input \(e_s\) has amplitude \(+1\) at the specified site \(s\).

A gate on edge \((j,j+1)\) applies \(R(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}\cos(\theta/2)&-\sin(\theta/2)\\ \sin(\theta/2)&\cos(\theta/2)\end{pmatrix}\) to the two amplitudes in increasing site order and fixes all other amplitudes. Every real angle is allowed.
conventions: One use of a gate costs one, regardless of angle. The empty circuit costs zero. There are no auxiliary sites, free sign changes or free permutations.
Preparation must output the particular signed vector \(x\). Only the action on \(e_s\) is prescribed. Assign minimum cost \(+\infty\) to an unreachable target.
question:
Find the exact minimum gate count for every \(x\) and \(s\). Give a lower bound that applies to every circuit, including those that visit sites outside the target support. Provide a construction meeting the bound whenever the target is reachable. Account for holes in the support, both signs of a target supported only at \(s\), and the one-site path.

As a check, on sites \(0,\ldots,7\) start at \(s=4\) and take \(x=(0,-3,0,0,0,0,4,0)/5\). What is the minimum count? More generally, when \(S\) has at least two sites and the source can be chosen, which choices of \(s\) minimize the count?

title: How much fidelity can a tree reach before the layer budget runs out?
assumptions: Let \(T\) be a finite nonempty tree rooted at \(r\). Each vertex \(v\) labels a real coordinate and has a known signed target amplitude \(a_v\), with \(\sum_v a_v^2=1\). The input is \(e_r\), the positive unit coordinate at the root.

One layer chooses a matching of tree edges. On an edge ordered as (parent, child) it may apply any block \(\begin{pmatrix}c&-s\\ s&c\end{pmatrix}\), with real \(c,s\) satisfying \(c^2+s^2=1\). Vertices outside the selected edges keep their amplitudes. There are at most \(d\ge0\) layers, where \(d\) is an integer.
conventions: Disjointness refers to vertices in the same layer. A vertex may participate again in a later layer. Empty layers and arbitrary choices of exact angles are allowed.

The score of an output \(y\) is its squared fidelity with \(a\), namely \(|\sum_v a_vy_v|^2\). A common sign is immaterial to the score. For a vertex \(v\), \(T_v\) consists of \(v\) and all its descendants.
question:
Determine the largest possible score for arbitrary \(T,a,d\). Give a recurrence with a table indexed by a vertex \(v\) and a remaining layer budget \(0\le t\le d\). Explain how to evaluate it in time polynomial in \(|V(T)|\) and \(d+1\), counting real arithmetic and comparisons as unit operations. You may use polynomial-time maximum-weight matching in a bipartite graph.

Prove an upper bound for every circuit, including circuits that revisit an edge or cancel an amplitude. Then show how to choose a circuit attaining your answer for signed targets. Address zero target mass among the sites reached by a schedule, a zero budget, and a tree consisting only of the root.

For a five-vertex example, the root \(r\) has children \(u,v\), with respective single children \(u',v'\). The only nonzero target entries are \(a_{u'}=1/\sqrt2\) and \(a_{v'}=-1/\sqrt2\). Compute the optimum at \(d=1,2,3\) and use it to assess the claim that all target mass within graph distance \(d\) can always be captured by depth \(d\).

title: When may a phase gate cross a permutation?
assumptions: Let \(X\) be a finite nonempty set with orthonormal basis \(\{|x\rangle:x\in X\}\). For a permutation \(p\) of \(X\) and a function \(a:X\to\mathbb T\), write \(M(a,p)|x\rangle=a(x)|p(x)\rangle\), where \(\mathbb T=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}\).
Write \(P_p=M(1,p)\) for pure routing and \(D_f=M(f,\mathrm{id})\) for a phase table \(f:X\to\mathbb T\).
conventions: Kets are columns. The rightmost factor acts first. Rows label outputs, and columns label inputs. Two operators agree up to global phase when one is a single constant of modulus one times the other on all inputs.
question:
Determine the output label and amplitude of \(M(b,q)M(a,p)|x\rangle\) for arbitrary weights and permutations. A circuit designer wants to move a phase gate to the input side of a routing gate. Determine the unique table \(g\) satisfying \(D_fP_p=P_pD_g\). When does keeping the original table give exact equality? When does keeping it give equality up to a single global phase? Prove both tests.

As a wiring check, let \(X=\{0,1\}^2\), write a label as \((c,t)\) with control bit first, and take \(p(c,t)=(c,t\mathbin{\oplus}c)\) and \(f(c,t)=e^{i\theta t}\) for real \(\theta\). Give the corrected input-side table and determine every angle for which the uncorrected reordering is valid, both exactly and up to a global phase. At \(\theta=\pi\), give a normalized two-term input for which the two uncorrected orderings produce orthogonal states, even though their computational-basis output probabilities agree on each computational-basis input.

title: Which phase references can be fixed on a permutation cycle?
assumptions: Let \(X\) be a finite nonempty set with a labeled orthonormal basis, and let \(p\) be a known permutation of \(X\). Write \(\mathbb T=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}\). Two devices act by \(U_a|x\rangle=a_x|p(x)\rangle\) and \(U_b|x\rangle=b_x|p(x)\rangle\), with \(a_x,b_x\in\mathbb T\).

A diagonal calibration has \(D|x\rangle=d_x|x\rangle\) with \(d_x\in\mathbb T\). A set \(S\subseteq X\) of reference labels requires \(d_s=\eta_s\) for specified \(\eta_s\in\mathbb T\). The set \(S\) may be empty.
conventions: The calibration equation is the exact operator identity \(U_b=DU_aD^\dagger\). A cycle follows the arrows \(x\mapsto p(x)\). Labels are fixed throughout, including labels in different cycles of the same length. A fixed point is a cycle of length one.
question:
Give a necessary and sufficient test, expressed in terms of the supplied edge weights and reference phases, for the calibration equation to have a solution. Construct every admissible \(D\) and describe all its freedom. Your test should work for cycles with no reference, one reference or several, and for fixed points. Show which information survives when each edge phase around a cycle can be adjusted through a change of basis.

A technician has recorded only the product of the edge weights around each labeled cycle. Show that matching these records can suffice when there are no fixed references yet fail after two phases on one cycle are prescribed. Give two devices with the same permutation and matching cycle records, along with reference values that are incompatible. Identify where the obstruction is visible along the cycle.

title: What can power traces recover about cycle phases?
assumptions: Let \(X\) be a finite labeled set of size \(N\geq1\), and let \(p\) be a known permutation. An unknown unitary acts on the labeled orthonormal basis by \(U|x\rangle=a_x|p(x)\rangle\), with \(|a_x|=1\). For each oriented cycle \(C\) of \(p\), let \(h_C=\prod_{x\in C}a_x\).

The data are exact complex numbers. Write \(t_n=\operatorname{tr}(U^n)\) for the global power traces. One may use Newton’s identities, which recover a monic degree-\(m\) polynomial from the first \(m\) power sums of its roots counted with multiplicity.
conventions: Cycles of length one are included. An arc follows the directed edge \(x\mapsto p(x)\). A cycle product belongs to its labeled cycle unless the requested output explicitly asks for an unordered multiset. The characteristic polynomial is \(\det(zI-U)\).
question:
Derive the characteristic polynomial and a formula for every positive power trace from the cycles and their edge weights. Suppose first that no two cycles have the same length. Using only \(t_1,\ldots,t_N\) and the known permutation, recover each \(h_C\) on its own cycle and prove your procedure works even when one cycle length divides another.

Can all global power traces determine even the multiset of products for each length for an arbitrary known permutation? Decide this already for one permutation with two fixed points and two transpositions. If recovery fails, construct two unit-modulus weight assignments on that same permutation. Verify equality of all their power traces and a difference of product multisets within at least one length, so that relabeling cycles of equal length cannot remove the ambiguity.

Now augment the readout as follows. For each occurring length \(\ell\), let \(m_\ell\) count its cycles and let \(P_\ell\) project onto the span of all basis vectors on those cycles. You receive \(\operatorname{tr}(P_\ell U^{k\ell})\) for \(1\leq k\leq m_\ell\). Determine what product data these reports recover for each length. Prove recovery with multiplicities and explain precisely when these reports assign the recovered products uniquely to the labeled cycles.
